title: Pip's Missing Blue Blankie
markdown:
In the tall Moonmallow Mountains, where moonlight played peek-a-boo with clouds, lived a little elf named Aster. Hair like the sky after rain, soft and pale. Eyes like morning dewdrops. He was a curious elf, always peeking behind toadstools.

Aster’s best friend was Pip. Pip was a little duckling. Feathers fluffy and yellow, like a dandelion puff. He waddled in a bouncy way that made everyone giggle. Pip loved Aster more than puddles, and that is a lot for a duckling.

One evening the sky turned soft pink and sleepy orange. The sun was tucking itself into bed. Aster snuggled into his mossy pillow, damp earth and quiet. Pip fluffed his chest, ready for dreams of tasty water bugs.

But Pip made a little “Quack?” His bright eyes looked around. Under his tiny acorn bed. Behind his mushroom stool. His soft blue blankie was gone. Utterly, completely, nowhere to be found. Pip nudged Aster. The quacks sounded worried.

“Oh dearie me,” whispered Aster. A little crinkle between his sparkling eyes. “Your very favourite blankie is missing? That won’t do at all.” He patted Pip’s fluffy head. “Don’t worry, Pip. We’ll find your blankie together.”

Aster gave a little hop. Pip gave a determined little quack. Their important mission began. The mountain paths were lit by glowworms, blinking like tiny happy stars, a twinkling carpet. Cool air. Wild thyme. Sweet night-blooming jasmine. They wandered near smooth rocks. The wind whispered, but only the ordinary kind, the kind that moves thyme and does not give speeches.

Rounding a bend near fragrant lavender, they heard humming. Beside a stone stall full of yummy cakes stood Gretchen the goblin. Gretchen was a baker. Cheeks round and rosy, like her apple tarts. A smile that could warm your toes. Hands dusted with flour, like soft snow. An apron with jam spots. She hummed a merry tune.

“Good evening, little ones,” Gretchen chirped, voice like tiny bells. “Are you out for an adventure? Or have you lost your way?” She tilted her head. Eyes twinkling kindly.

“Not lost, friendly Gretchen,” Aster said, polite and clear. “But my friend Pip’s favourite blankie is missing. It’s soft. It’s blue, like the summer sky.”

Pip gave a hopeful “Quack?”

Gretchen tapped her chin, round and rosy.

“A missing blankie, you say? Hmm. I did see something blue flutter by. Near the big sleepy boulder by my cake stall. It looked as if it wanted to smell my Honey-Dew Drops.” She winked. Flour flew from her nose.

Aster and Pip hurried to the sleepy boulder. Hearts thumping with hope. Tucked under soft green moss, next to a plate of Honey-Dew Drops, was Pip’s blue blankie. It had just come for a sniff of Gretchen’s baking. Next to the blankie was a tiny cake, a sweet surprise from Gretchen, the perfect size for a little duckling, with a tiny candied violet.

Pip let out a long happy quack. He nudged the blankie. He snuggled into its familiar softness. Honey-sweet. Aster smiled. Warm and cozy in his chest. He looked at Gretchen and gave a grateful nod. She waved her floury hand and kept humming.

And so Pip snuggled in his blue blankie, with a tiny cake for a treat. Aster and Pip walked home. The glowworms blinked them goodnight. The moon peeked from a cloud with warm silvery light. Pip, blankie held tight, drifted off, dreaming of flying through blue skies and eating tiny delicious cakes. The stall kept its jammy smell. The boulder kept its moss. The blankie, at last, kept Pip.
